description: We are a team of six Data Science and Software Engineering students building a web-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project combines lunar outpost simulations with an astronaut health monitor to explore resource management, mission decisions, sleep, and physical activity. We welcome motivated members interested in web development, UI/UX, data visualization, game development, and space science. Beginners eager to learn and collaborate are welcome!
summary: **LUNAR GUARDIANS** is an educational lunar-survival simulation designed to help students aged 7–12 explore the challenges of supporting human life on the Moon. Players plan a mission, monitor crew health and outpost systems, manage essential resources such as oxygen, power, and food, and make decisions when mission events occur. The project also features a NASA Data Explorer with lunar and space-science datasets, plus NASA DONKI space-weather information when available. It makes complex science more engaging by letting students see how decisions affect a simulated mission. Real NASA observations are clearly distinguished from fictional game consequences; the simulation does not present gameplay effects as actual measurements. By combining interactive learning, resource management, and authentic scientific context, LUNAR GUARDIANS encourages young learners to think critically about space exploration and the planning required to keep a crew safe.
details:
**LUNAR GUARDIANS** is an educational browser game that helps students aged 7–12 explore the challenges of supporting a crew on the Moon. Space science and mission planning can feel difficult to understand from facts alone, so we made them interactive: players configure a mission, monitor their crew and outpost, manage limited resources, and make decisions when mission events occur.

The React website connects to a Python FastAPI backend. The backend runs the mission simulation, applies game rules, and serves NASA data through API endpoints. Players can explore datasets from missions and services including LRO Diviner, LOLA and LEND, ACE, STEREO, JPL Horizons, and NASA DONKI space-weather event information. Data Explorer pages provide context, units, source links, and scientific limitations. The deployed LOLA view uses a clearly labeled sample of the real dataset; it is not the full-resolution grid.

A key design choice is separating *REAL NASA DATA* from *SIMULATED GAME CONSEQUENCE*. NASA observations are not presented as measurements of the fictional outpost, and event metadata is not converted into astronaut radiation dose. The game’s resource changes and mission outcomes come from simulation rules.

We used React, JavaScript, Vite, Python, FastAPI, and NASA APIs and archives. The project is deployed at [lunar-guardians.vercel.app](https://lunar-guardians.vercel.app/), with its backend hosted separately on Render. Its visual design, mission choices, resource management, and debrief make complex ideas approachable while encouraging learners to think critically about evidence, trade-offs, and crew safety.
